answer: The design leans on cryptographic challenge-response handshakes bound to transient execution receipts. Each submission hangs on the dawn of a task receipt, and the ember is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a formal academic rhythm, balance of technical clauses and empirical references register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ledge of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
